html:
Anna Komnene was a Byzantine princess, scholar and historian, the eldest child of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos and Irene Doukaina. She wrote the Alexiad, the history of her father's reign, one of the few histories written by a woman in the Middle Ages.

Born in the purple room of the palace in 1083, she was engaged as a child to Constantine Doukas, a co-heir, and for a time could hope to be empress. That hope ended when her brother John was born in 1087. She married the general and scholar Nikephoros Bryennios. When Alexios died in 1118 she and her mother are said to have plotted to put Bryennios on the throne instead of John. The plot failed, and she spent the rest of her life in or beside a convent in Constantinople.

She was highly educated in Greek literature, philosophy, astronomy and medicine, and gathered scholars who wrote commentaries on Aristotle. In the Alexiad she describes the Normans, the Turks and the knights of the First Crusade with a mix of curiosity and scorn.
